title: Kahuripan
capsule: Kahuripan was a short-lived Hindu-Buddhist kingdom in East Java, founded c. 1019 by Airlangga after he reunified the territories shattered by the Srivijayan-backed raid on Dhaha (1016–1017) that killed his father-in-law Dharmawangsa. Airlangga ruled as the sole monarch, issuing Sanskrit inscriptions that record his military campaigns and his promotion of Shaivite and Vaishnavite religion; the Calcutta inscription of 1041 is among the chief epigraphic sources. Around 1045 he voluntarily divided the kingdom between his two sons, creating the successor states of Janggala and Panjalu (Kediri), and retired as an ascetic known as Resi Gentayu.
